steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Keeper Elias Quinn awoke before dawn, as he had every morning for twenty-four years. He brewed coffee in the tiny galley of Sunders Point Light, listening to gulls wheel in the gray predawn hush. The sea breathed against the black rocks below, a slow, familiar pulse that matched the old man’s own heartbeat.

At 5:13 a.m., right on schedule, the beacon extinguished with a soft click. Night’s duties complete, Elias climbed the iron stairs to the lantern room for inspection. Salt etched the glass in feathery patterns, marking where storms had flung up spray. With a rag and patience, he polished each pane until sunrise flooded the chamber with molten gold.

Down in the keeper’s log he wrote:

“Fog thin. Swell mild. One fishing sloop outbound. Light in order.”

Routine words—yet they formed a quiet conversation with the future, a way of telling tomorrow’s keepers that everything, for this brief dawn, was well.

At noon the supply boat arrived. Young Mara Delaney leapt onto the landing, her apprentice badge still new. She carried fresh lamp oil, letters, and news of the mainland. Elias offered her coffee, and together they watched the sea, horizon bright as promise.

One day, he knew, she would write the log in her own clear hand. When that time came, the lighthouse would not mourn his absence; it would simply keep shining, as steadfast and forgiving as the tide itself.
